title: Ship the static site
prompt: Put the steps for Lantern's first production deploy of the front end in a working order. The bucket stays private and the site is served only through CloudFront on `https://lantern.example`. Finish the build-and-S3 work first, then do the certificate, CloudFront and DNS work.
hints: You can't upload files you haven't built, or into a bucket that doesn't exist.
The distribution needs the certificate when you attach the custom domain, and the bucket policy needs the distribution's ARN.
DNS goes last before testing, so visitors never land on a half-configured distribution.
explanation: Build first so there is something to upload, then create the private bucket and sync the files with their cache headers. The certificate must exist (and be validated) in us-east-1 before you can attach `lantern.example` to the distribution. The distribution must exist before the bucket policy, because the policy's `AWS:SourceArn` condition names the distribution's ARN. Only when CloudFront can read the bucket do you point DNS at it, and the final check proves both halves: the site loads through CloudFront and the bucket refuses direct requests with 403.

items.build: Run `npm run build` to produce the `dist/` folder.
items.bucket: Create the private `lantern-site-prod` bucket in Lantern's Region, with Block Public Access left on.
items.upload: Upload `dist/` with `aws s3 sync`, long cache headers for hashed assets and `no-cache` for `index.html`.
items.cert: Request and DNS-validate an ACM certificate for `lantern.example` in `us-east-1`.
items.distribution: Create the CloudFront distribution with origin access control, `index.html` as default root object and the certificate attached.
items.policy: Add the bucket policy that allows `s3:GetObject` for `cloudfront.amazonaws.com` with an `AWS:SourceArn` condition for this distribution.
items.dns: Create alias A and AAAA records for `lantern.example` pointing at the distribution.
items.verify: Check that `https://lantern.example` loads and that the bucket's direct URL returns 403.
